faq.q: Should you tailor your resume for every job application?
faq.a: Yes, and the reason is mechanical rather than stylistic: applicant tracking systems read a resume against one specific job description. SkillDrift keeps a master copy and produces a tailored version per posting, so the emphasis matches the role without you rebuilding the document.

faq.q: Does SkillDrift invent things to put on your resume?
faq.a: No. It re-emphasises and reorders what you already supplied and it asks you when something is missing. Every figure on a tailored version is one you gave it.

faq.q: What does tailoring a resume cost?
faq.a: A tailored version is 18 credits. A full outcome rewrite is 70. An ATS rewrite is 70. Every new account is granted 160 credits, and the diagnosis itself is free.

faq.q: How do you know if your resume is ATS friendly?
faq.a: Run it through the free ATS score checker. SkillDrift returns your resume readiness as a four level band, with the specific problems named, and it does not require an account.

sections.heading: Why does listing your responsibilities weaken your resume?

cards.title: The duty version
cards.body: “Led the engineering team and was involved in technical strategy.”

cards.title: The outcome version
cards.body: “Grew engineering from 9 to 34 across three squads; cut median deploy time from 40 minutes to 6 and halved release failures.”

routes.relatedHeading: How do you turn a duty into an outcome on a resume?

faq.q: Why does listing your responsibilities weaken your resume?
faq.a: Because a responsibility describes the job, not you. Two people with the same title write the same bullet. An outcome, with a number attached, is the only part of a resume that separates one candidate from another, and it is also what an applicant tracking system can weight.

faq.q: Will an AI resume rewrite invent things about you?
faq.a: No. SkillDrift asks you for anything it does not already have on your resume, and every figure in the rewritten version is one you supplied.

faq.q: What does a resume rewrite cost?
faq.a: A full outcome rewrite is 70 credits and an ATS rewrite is 70. Every new account is granted 160 credits. The diagnosis, including your ATS readiness band, is free.

faq.q: How do you turn a duty into an outcome on a resume?
faq.a: Take the duty, ask what changed because of it, and put the change first. SkillDrift does this line by line and asks you for the figure when it is missing rather than estimating one.

faq.q: How do you know if you are a good match for a job?
faq.a: By reading your resume against that specific job description rather than against a job title. SkillDrift returns a match out of 100 for each role, with a band from Stretch through Workable and Good fit to Strong fit, and names the skills that produced the number.

faq.q: Is job matching free?
faq.a: Yes. Job and internship matches are scored for free, and a basic analysis of any individual role costs nothing. A detailed job analysis is 37 credits.

faq.q: What does a job match score out of 100 actually measure?
faq.a: The overlap between the skills the role requires and the skills your resume evidences, weighted by how central each one is to that role. Every point traces to a named skill, so the score can be interrogated rather than trusted.

faq.q: Does the score change as you learn?
faq.a: Yes. Match scores are recomputed against the same job descriptions when your skills change, so closing a named gap moves the number on every role that needed it.

routes.relatedHeading: How do you decide what to learn next?

faq.q: Why do people not finish online courses?
faq.a: Because the unit is too large. A forty hour course asks for a commitment before it has proved it is the right thing to learn. A sprint built from a named gap in your own report is short enough to finish and specific enough to be worth finishing.

faq.q: What happens when you finish a sprint?
faq.a: The gap closes and everything downstream re-scores. Your readiness percentage moves, jobs are re-matched out of 100 against your new skills, and the certificate is written into your resume automatically rather than being something you have to add.

faq.q: What does a certificate cost, and where does it go?
faq.a: The learning content is free. Building the roadmap is 50 credits and the certificate is 50, so a first course and a first certificate together cost 100 against the 160 credits every new account is granted.

faq.q: How do you decide what to learn next?
faq.a: Start from the gap that moves your readiness most, which SkillDrift ranks for you rather than leaving to a catalogue. Each sprint maps to one named missing skill for the role you actually want.

routes.title: Does SkillDrift work? The evidence, and its limits | SkillDrift
routes.description: Every outcome number SkillDrift publishes, what each one counts, and what it does not prove. Company reported, method stated, none of it independently audited.
routes.h1: Does SkillDrift actually work, and how would you know?

hero.standfirst: SkillDrift publishes five outcome numbers. All five are company reported, measured from our own product data, and none of them has been independently audited. This page sets out what SkillDrift can demonstrate from its own product data, what it deliberately does not measure, and what would be needed to prove more. The short version: we can show that readiness scores move as people learn, and that resumes and certificates update automatically when they do. We cannot yet show that a higher SkillDrift score causes a job offer, and we do not claim it.

sections.heading: What can SkillDrift actually prove today?
paragraphs: Three things, all of them measured inside the product rather than reported by users. First, that a readiness score changes over time for people who complete learning, because the score is recomputed from the same resume every time it is read. Second, that a completed course writes a certificate into the resume without the user doing anything, because that write is the product mechanic rather than a manual step. Third, that a job match score out of 100 moves when the underlying skills change, because the match is recomputed against the same job description.
All three are statements about the machinery. None of them is a statement about employment.

sections.heading: What does SkillDrift count as a result, and what does it deliberately not count?
paragraphs: We count things the product does: a readiness score recomputed, a named gap closed, a certificate written into a resume, a tailored version generated, a job match re-scored. We do not count applications sent, interviews attended, offers received or salary changes, because we do not observe any of them.

A user can be hired the week after they close a gap and we would never know, and a user can close every gap and not get hired. Anyone claiming a career platform has measured your employment outcome is either integrated with your employer or guessing.

sections.heading: Is any of this independently verified?
paragraphs: No. Every number on this page is measured by SkillDrift from SkillDrift’s own data, and none of it has been audited by a third party. That is a real limitation and it applies to every AI career product currently on the market, ours included.

The reason to state it rather than bury it is that a score you cannot interrogate is worth less than a score you can: our numbers are worth exactly as much as the method behind them, which is why the method is on this page.

sections.heading: What would actually prove it, and what would have to be true?
paragraphs: Outcome validation needs three things we do not have yet: a large enough cohort followed for long enough, a control group of comparable people not using the product, and a reliable signal of what happened to them afterwards. The honest position is that none of the three exists today.
What we can do in the meantime is publish the method for every number we quote, correct anything found wrong, and never present a company reported figure as an independent one.

routes.description: SkillDrift closes the loop between the job you want and the skills you have: score the gap, close it, and let your resume update itself as you go.

hero.standfirst: SkillDrift closes the loop between the job you want and the skills you have: score the gap, close it, and let your resume update itself as you go.

sections.heading: Career advice is everywhere. Career measurement is not.
paragraphs: Most people looking for work are not short of advice. They are short of a number: some honest measure of the distance between where they are and the role they want, and a sense of which move closes the most of it.

Every tool in this market hands you one arc of the circle. A course library that knows nothing about the job you want. A resume builder that formats what you already wrote. A job board that ranks by recency rather than fit. Each is useful; none of them tells you whether anything is working.

SkillDrift exists to join them. Upload a resume, and the gap between you and a target role is scored out of 100. The roadmap that closes it is built from that score. Finish a sprint and the certificate writes itself back into the resume, the score re-scores itself free, and better roles unlock. Then it goes round again.
